claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you tell me the **names and ages of all the children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 10 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather a few more details about your circumstances.

**Are you the parent or guardian with whom Alex normally lives?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

**Does Alex live with you for part of the week or at certain times, or is there no regular arrangement where Alex stays with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no regular arrangement - Alex doesn't stay with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you providing that clarity.

**Are you currently responsible for providing for Alex's day-to-day care and maintenance, even though Alex doesn't live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I do help out a bit - I contribute towards things like clothes and bits and pieces for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. That's helpful context.

**To clarify further, do you have formal legal responsibility for Alex (such as through a court order or legal guardianship), or is your contribution more informal?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's more informal - I just help out financially when I can.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question to help complete the picture.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? Are you a UK citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK resident, yes - I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 10 years old and does not live with you
- There is no regular arrangement for Alex to stay with you
- Your financial contribution towards Alex's care is informal
- You do not have formal legal responsibility for Alex
- You are a UK resident

**Under UK Child Benefit rules, the claimant must be responsible for a child, which means the child must normally live with them or there must be a formal arrangement in place (such as shared care with a court order).** Since Alex does not live with you and there is no formal legal responsibility or regular arrangement, you would not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

The key reason is that Child Benefit requires the claimant to be responsible for the child, which means the child must normally live with you or there must be a formal arrangement in place (such as a court-ordered shared care arrangement). Since Alex doesn't live with you and there's no formal legal responsibility or regular arrangement, you don't meet the eligibility requirements.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you obtain formal legal responsibility or Alex comes to live with you—you would be able to reapply.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
